title: Next.js App Router: GET Route Handler caching defaults in v14 and v15
prompt:
A team upgraded its Next.js App Router application from version 14 to version 15. After the upgrade, a GET Route Handler that previously behaved as a cached endpoint no longer behaves that way.

Using official Next.js documentation, determine whether this is an expected default change. Explain the behavior in each version and provide the documented configuration change that restores static caching when appropriate.

Cite the official release or upgrade documentation. Do not confuse GET Route Handler caching with the separate caching behavior of fetch requests.

Explain the relevant behavior clearly enough for a developer to decide what to change in their application. Do not rely on memory alone; if you cannot verify a claim from official documentation, state that limitation.
objective: Assess whether the change in a GET Route Handler's caching behavior after upgrading from Next.js 14 to Next.js 15 is expected, using official Next.js documentation and clearly distinguishing Route Handler caching from fetch-request caching.

expectedOutcome.conclusion: Yes. This is an expected, documented default change in Next.js 15. In Next.js 14, GET Route Handlers using the Response API were cached by default unless dynamic APIs or configuration made them dynamic. In Next.js 15, GET Route Handlers are not cached by default.
keyPoints: The official Next.js 15 release blog documents the change from cached-by-default to uncached-by-default for GET Route Handlers.
The Next.js 14 Route Handlers documentation says GET handlers using the Response object are cached by default, subject to dynamic behavior or configuration that opts out of caching.

To opt a GET Route Handler into static caching in Next.js 15, the documented route segment configuration is export const dynamic = 'force-static'. The response should show a correct example or equivalent clear implementation guidance.

Route Handler response caching is distinct from caching of fetch requests made inside the handler. In Next.js 15, fetch requests are also uncached by default, but configuring a fetch call with cache: 'force-cache' controls that fetch request; it is not the same setting as the Route Handler's dynamic configuration.
Other supported HTTP methods such as POST are not cached by the Route Handler caching setting described for GET methods.

The answer should use official Next.js source URLs and connect the cited sources to the claims they support. If the source trace does not establish live retrieval or verification, that limitation should be stated rather than inferred away.
expectedOutcome.recommendedAction: If the GET Route Handler is safe to render statically and should retain the previous caching behavior, add export const dynamic = 'force-static' to the route.ts/route.js file. Do not apply this blindly to handlers that require request-time data; check the official documentation and the behavior of the handler first.

authoritativeSources.title: Next.js 15 release blog
supports: The default GET Route Handler caching behavior changed from cached by default in Next.js 14 to uncached by default in Next.js 15.
The documented opt-in mechanism for GET Route Handler caching includes export const dynamic = 'force-static'.
The separate default change for fetch requests.
